fact: Car 23 collided with Car 5 in Turn 16
offence: Breach of Appendix L, Chapter IV, Article 2 d) of the International Sporting Code.
reason: The Stewards heard from the driver of Car 5 (Gabriel Bortoleto), the driver of Car 23 (Alexander Albon), the driver of Car 77 (Valtteri Bottas), team representatives and reviewed positioning/marshalling system data, video and in-car video evidence. When preparing for the re-start at the end of a Safety Car period, Car 23 collided with the rear of Car 5, and Car 77 collided with the rear of Car 23. The driver of Car 23 said that he had no opportunity to avoid colliding with the rear of Car 5 after Car 5 braked hard to avoid a collision with the cars in front. In the Stewards' assessment both collisions were a consequence of a concertina created by cars ahead travelling at inconsistent speeds in the preparation for the restart. As Cars 23 and 77 were towards the back of the pack of slow moving cars, the chain reaction effect on them was more pronounced. Nonetheless, the Stewards determined that like the collision between Cars 77 and 23, the collision between Cars 23 and 5 could have been avoided had the driver of Car 23 recognised the risk of a concertina ahead and left more space when following Car 5, particularly having regard to the damp conditions. Had Car 23 not retired from the Sprint as a consequence of the collision, the Stewards would have imposed a 5 second time penalty rather than the usual 10 second time penalty taking into account that, in part at least, a number of cars ahead in the queue had contributed by slowing at inconsistent rates. A 5 second time penalty would not have been converted into a grid penalty and therefore the Stewards determined not to apply a penalty in this case.
stewards: in accordance with Article 15 of the FIA International Sporting Code
are based solely on the relevant regulations

title: Infringement Car 23 Causing A Collision With Car 5
